dialogue.user: Those all look promising! Can you tell me more about the **Oboz Women's Bridger Mid B-Dry Waterproof Hiking Boots, Wide Walnut 6.5**? What kind of materials are they made of, and are they known for being comfortable?
dialogue.agent:
The **Oboz Women's Bridger Mid B-Dry Waterproof Hiking Boots, Wide Walnut 6.5** are made with a waterproof nubuck leather upper and abrasion-resistant fabric. They feature a moisture-wicking nylon mesh lining, a B-Dry breathable membrane to keep moisture out, and a PU heel pod for ergonomic support. The O FIT Insole combines plush foam, a structured high-density heel and arch cup, and a moisture-wicking Soft Touch top layer with medium-density EVA foam throughout. The boots also have a dual-density EVA midsole for extra cushioning, a non-marking rubber outsole with multi-directional traction, and a board-lasted design for stability. Here are some top reviews:

1. **Love Oboz and Love These Boots!**
   - Rating: 5.0
   - "I had never heard of Oboz before until I ordered a pair of boots in a different style a few years ago. I fell in love with this brand and when I saw this style, which looked like it had a bit more ankle support, I just had to order them. Straight out of the box, I couldn't believe how light they were. Even with thick socks, they were easy to pull on. I usually wear a size 7 in a shoe, but I ordered a 8.5 in these boots because they seem to run just a little bit small and my toe kept hitting the front of the boot. I knew I needed a larger size in addition to the toe thing because my feet swell when out hiking. The 8.5 fits wonderfully and allows me room to wear thick hiking socks with a little bit of wiggle room, but snug enough to not have a loose heel. I've worn these boots out in the field on a number of different occasions and have not had a single blister or hot spot. Plus, they have good ankle support for me and the tread is sturdy and has kept me me from slipping in wet or slick situations. I also really like the bright red color I ordered. I did, however, have to replace the rounded laces with flat laces in order to keep the laces from coming untied. I have this issue with pretty much all of my hiking boots and really wish hiking boots would come with flat laces in general. Once I replaced the round laces with flat ones, I had no more problems. As for arch support - I have flat feet so I can't really tell you much about that, except that my feet are comfortable and the boots are not heavy and clunky like others I have in my closet. I know how quickly styles come and go, and I like this particular style so much, I ordered another pair just to have after this pair wears out."

2. **First pair of Oboz**
   - Rating: 5.0
   - "I tried these boots on at the local outfitters. Loved them but couldn't bring myself to spend the asking price of $160. The lady at the outfitter said her and her daughter wear them often and have done many hikes. They like these boots/shoes so much that they carry a great selection. She did recommend getting a half size larger to allow the extra room in toe area for up and down trails, otherwise you would end up with sore toes.... which is exactly what was happing with my current pair of hikers. She also mentioned to tie them a little loose around the ankle until they are broken in. I ordered these about a month ago. Second day I had them I went to appalachian trail for two mile waterfall hike. I purposely stepped in water at the falls and NO wet feet! I walk 2-13 miles a day and have had no sores or rubbing. They wear well and I have found now that they are my go to boot! Getting a pair for my husband!"

3. **Best Hiking Boots**
   - Rating: 5.0
   - "I LOVE these hiking boots. I hike/trail walk 6+ miles a day and from day 1 with these boots they have been extremely comfortable (and I have plantar fasciitis so thats saying something). I recently bought Anuh because they were lighter in weight but they are stiff and the insoles are not very comfortable. This is my second pair of Oboz Women's Bridger B-DRY Hiking Boot and I will continue to buy them. My first pair lasted 3+ years and although the boots still look and feel great they are no longer waterproof so I needed to replace them."

Would you like to know more about any other boots?

top_reviews.title: Love Oboz and Love These Boots!
top_reviews.text: I had never heard of Oboz before until I ordered a pair of boots in a different style a few years ago.  I fell in love with this brand and when I saw this style, which looked like it had a bit more ankle support, I just had to order them.  Straight out of the box, I couldn't believe how light they were.  Even with thick socks, they were easy to pull on.  I usually wear a size 7 in a shoe, but I ordered a 8.5 in these boots because they seem to run just a little bit small and my toe kept hitting the front of the boot. I knew I needed a larger size in addition to the toe thing because my feet swell when out hiking. The 8.5 fits wonderfully and allows me room to wear thick hiking socks with a little bit of wiggle room, but snug enough to not have a loose heel.  I've worn these boots out in the field on a number of different occasions and have not had a single blister or hot spot.  Plus, they have good ankle support for me and the tread is sturdy and has kept me me from slipping in wet or slick situations.  I also really like the bright red color I ordered.  I did, however, have to replace the rounded laces with flat laces in order to keep the laces from coming untied.  I have this issue with pretty much all of my hiking boots and really wish hiking boots would  come with flat laces in general.  Once I replaced the round laces with flat ones, I had no more problems.  As for arch support - I have flat feet so I can't really tell you much about that, except that my feet are  comfortable and the boots are not heavy and clunky like others I have in my closet.  I know how quickly styles come and go, and I like this particular style so much, I ordered another pair just to have after this pair wears out.

top_reviews.title: First pair of Oboz
top_reviews.text: I tried these boots on at the local outfitters.  Loved them but couldn't bring myself to spend the asking price of $160.  The lady at the outfitter said her and her daughter wear them often and have done many hikes.  They like these boots//shoes so much that they carry a great selection.  She did recommend getting a half size larger to allow the extra room in toe area for up and down trails, otherwise you would end up with sore toes.... which is exactly what was happing with my current pair of hikers. She also mentioned to tie them a little loose around the ankle until they are broken in.  I ordered these about a month ago. Second day I had them I went to appalachian trail for two mile waterfall hike. I purposely stepped in water at the falls and NO wet feet!  I walk 2-13 miles a day and have had no sores or rubbing.  They wear well and I have found now that they are my go to boot!  Getting a pair for my husband!

top_reviews.title: Best Hiking Boots
top_reviews.text: I LOVE these hiking boots.  I hike/trail walk 6+ miles a day and from day 1 with these boots they have been extremely comfortable (and I have plantar fasciitis so thats saying something).  I recently bought Anuh because they were lighter in weight but they are stiff and the insoles are not very comfortable.  This is my second pair of Oboz Women's Bridger B-DRY Hiking Boot and I will continue to buy them.  My first pair lasted 3+ years and although the boots still look and feel great they are no longer waterproof so I needed to replace them.
